items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Tom Albers; the name is only mentioned by the interviewer in relation to Mooney Martin.

ctx.x: They sure they could have made a bunch of, all Al Travis would have had to do was continue the bookers from Florida back into New York and we possibly would have gone into all of the major, major spots because he knew how to sell it. That is really weird to me, you know, that a man could be such a successful salesman. And he's so crooked and so no good. And if he leaves the few bucks that he would have been doing, he would have been doing it. He would have built that up into a repeat there. That's going to be a…

I'm interested in baseball a little bit. I don't know much about it, but you do. I've always been fascinated in talking to people. Like, I don't know if you know Mooney Martin or not, but he used to play baseball long before your time and he's a friend of Tom Albers, but he would tell me about the different teams, Algiers they had, and they had teams out in the country. You know, and I hear different people talk about that. Well, New Orleans was a big baseball

town and I used to go to the old Crescent Star Park, which was back in town, as you used to say, and went on the outside for a foul ball to come over and scramble with the other kids and get the ball and go in. What was the first time? Somewhere in back town. I can't remember the exact location. Look it up. And I'm sure some of the more at least can pin-pink the question so far. What about the Dixie Park? I don't know anything about the Dixie Park.
